finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL server-side. The only check is a https:// prefix, and axios follows redirects, so the scheme check and any destination restriction are bypassable. The response size is returned to the attacker, giving a blind SSRF oracle.

trace.note: typeof string and startsWith('https://') only; no host or IP allowlist
axios.get(url) with default redirect following; attacker picks host, port, path
res.json({bytes: img.data.length}) returns response size as an oracle

finding.guards_checked: typeof string check; https:// prefix check (raw string, no URL parse, no host check); no redirect restriction; no DNS or private-IP check; no authentication on route. Redirect from https to http or internal address is not validated.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is typeof url !== "string" || !url.startsWith("https://") at server.js:11, a scheme prefix check with no host or IP restriction. No authentication on the route (server.js:9), and no redirect or private-address validation before axios.get at server.js:14.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10) reaches axios.get(url) at server.js:14 after only an https:// prefix check (server.js:11), which does not restrict host, IP, or redirect targets, and the response size is returned at server.js:15, so the SSRF is confirmed.
